what: The score combines exact insertion distance with four customer-priority signals: depot-distance urgency, capacity filling that strengthens as the route fills, a reward for retaining a close feasible continuation, and a penalty when the insertion narrowly blocks a strongly related customer. Geographic affinity is the depot saving d(0,c)+d(0,j)-d(c,j). The chosen position is governed primarily by insertion delta because all priority terms are position-independent. Each call costs O(len(current_route)+len(unassigned)) time and O(1) extra space.
why: Farthest-customer seeding benefits from adding customers that create substantial depot savings rather than repeatedly postponing remote customers. Capacity-aware terms address both relatively uniform demands and instances containing customers that consume most of a vehicle: they encourage useful filling while avoiding choices that leave unusable capacity or split a close pair merely because one demand no longer fits. Exact insertion delta remains dominant for local ordering and gives intra-route 2-opt a short, coherent tour to refine. The constants are scale-independent but heuristic; pair affinity is only a one-customer lookahead, residual capacity is not solved as a packing problem, and no empirical improvement is claimed without evaluation on held-out families.
